name: When should a homeowner choose a kitchen addition over reconfiguring an existing layout?

mainEntity.name: When should a homeowner choose a kitchen addition over reconfiguring an existing layout?

acceptedAnswer.text: You should consider a kitchen addition when your current kitchen cannot support everyday cooking, foot traffic, or essential storage, and adjacent interior rooms cannot be reconfigured. If your home has a cramped floor plan, lacks space for an island or pantry, or feels isolated from entertaining spaces, building outward provides custom square footage. It is also an ideal solution if you love your neighborhood and property but have simply outgrown your current layout.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose an addition when interior walls cannot be moved to create needed storage and workflow, and your property has sufficient exterior yard space.
